newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Re says Euro floods cost 150 mln Sfr.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Re says Euro floods cost 150 mln Sfr.

text.p: Swiss Reinsurance Co said catastrophic flooding in Germany, Poland and the Czech Republic would cost it 150 million Swiss francs in direct payments based on initial cautious estimates.
"For the company, the loss corresponds to a medium-seized event, such as might be expected once every two years, and for which cover is provided by adequate provisions," Swiss Re said in a statement.
"The floods in the affected areas may be regarded as a 'hundred-year event' and have grave consequences for the local populations and economies," the company said.
Swiss Re, the world's second-biggest reinsurance group after Munich Re , said it was exposed to damage from the flooding in July and August because it had a leading market position in Central Europe.
It said the figure of 150 million Swiss francs ($97.9 million) was based on information available so far but added that losses were still being evaluated.
"Swiss Re experts have travelled to the flood-stricken areas to make more detailed investigations," Swiss Re said.
Surging rivers killed more than 100 people in the Czech Republic and Poland and devastated vast swathes of land, towns, farms and villages there and in Germany.
